newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mixed ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mixed ahead of FOMC.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed on a mixed note, with the key yen contract ending slightly higher on late short-covering, traders said.
While June yen rallied above its pivot point of $0.008668, weak longs liquidated positions in marks and Swiss francs and sent the June contracts in those key currencies lower.

One floor trader said longs were nervous to hold positions overnight in front of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting. There is a 50-50 chance the FOMC will raise the U.S. Federal funds rate on Tuesday, and thereby make the dollar slightly more attractive to investors.

According to a Reuters monthly asset allocation survey, global fund managers are swapping assets into Japanese equities and cash, and U.K.-based fund managers showed an increased underweight position in U.S. equities.
The strategists said Japan was seen at a favorable point in its economic cycle compared with the U.S. and most of Europe.

The yen's rise against the mark reflects that outlook, several yen futures traders said. They said June yen and mark pit trade has been influenced by the overnight moves in the mark/yen cash cross rate.
"You are starting to see some people take profits, because the cross rate has moved out so much," one floor trader said.
June yen set a 4-1/2-month high of $0.008760 last Thursday after the dollar/yen fell below 115.00 spot.
"I'm a little more neutral about yen, but I think the European currencies are going to continue to move lower," another pit trader said.
"The yen had a three-week move over three days," he said. "It's a little tired."
June Canadian dollars inched slightly higher to $0.7312, but below the intraday resistance level of $0.7318.
Meanwhile, long liquidation pushed June marks below support at $0.5877, which was the low for May, and through support at $0.5866, which was roughly equivalent to 1.7080 spot marks.

At the end of pit trade, June yen was up $0.000003 at $0.008683, marks off $0.0053 at $0.5868, Swiss francs down $0.0031 to $0.7030, sterling up $0.0036 at $1.6396, Canadian dollars rose $0.0014 to $0.7307, Australian dollars lost $0.0004 to $0.7747, and pesos gained $0.000225 to $0.125375.
